passages.text: EARTH, Theory of, an account of the formation of the globe and of the changes it has since undergone.
According to the sacred chronology, the earth was created about 4000 years before the Christian era, which most writers of theories endeavour to reconcile with the appearances of nature.
Dr Burnet supposed the original earth to have been a smooth crust without mountains or seas, which, breaking at the deluge, let out the waters of the abyss.
Mr Buffon conjectures that the earth was struck off from the sun by a comet, and has been cooling ever since, a period which he computes at about 75,000 years.

Dr Hutton of Edinburgh holds that the present continents are formed of the ruins of former ones, worn down by water and raised again by subterraneous heat; and that in this succession he finds no vestige of a beginning, no prospect of an end.
The strata of the earth are thought by most naturalists to have been deposited all at once by the waters of the deluge.
The age of Earth is estimated to be 4.54 billion years, with an uncertainty of about 1%. The figure comes from radiometric dating of meteorites and of the oldest minerals on Earth.
In the 17th century, James Ussher calculated from the Bible that the Earth was created in 4004 BC.
Georges-Louis Leclerc, Comte de Buffon, estimated from the cooling of heated iron spheres that the Earth was about 75,000 years old.
James Hutton argued in the late 18th century that slow processes seen today, such as erosion and the raising of land, had shaped the Earth over immense periods of time.
The Earth formed together with the Sun and the other planets from a disc of dust and gas around the young Sun.
Sedimentary rock layers built up slowly over very long periods; their order and the radiometric dating of volcanic layers within them give their ages.
In the 19th century, Lord Kelvin estimated from the Earth's cooling an age of 20 to 400 million years. His figure was too low because he did not know about heating by radioactivity.

reasons: The 1797 entry is a survey of theories of the earth's formation; no single Wikipedia article has the same scope.
Age of Earth matches its central question, and names the same people: Ussher's chronology, Buffon, Hutton.
Rerank 0.72 is below our 0.75 threshold for a strong match. History of Earth and Neptunism each cover a part.

alignments.label: Six thousand years

britannica.quote: the earth was created about 4000 years before the Christian era

wikipedia.quote: The age of Earth is estimated to be 4.54 billion years

alignments.note: Off by a factor of about 750,000.

alignments.label: The sacred chronology

wikipedia.quote: James Ussher calculated from the Bible that the Earth was created in 4004 BC

alignments.note: Both describe the same date from the same source. Wikipedia treats it as history, not as an age.

alignments.label: Burnet's smooth earth

britannica.quote: a smooth crust without mountains or seas, which, breaking at the deluge, let out the waters of the abyss

alignments.note: Inference: Wikipedia's account of the earth's formation has no smooth first crust and no flood.

alignments.label: Struck off by a comet

britannica.quote: struck off from the sun by a comet

wikipedia.quote: The Earth formed together with the Sun and the other planets from a disc of dust and gas

alignments.note: Buffon was right that the earth and sun are linked, wrong about the comet.

alignments.label: Buffon's 75,000 years

britannica.quote: a period which he computes at about 75,000 years

wikipedia.quote: estimated from the cooling of heated iron spheres that the Earth was about 75,000 years old

alignments.note: Both report the same figure. It was bold for its time and still far too young.

alignments.label: Hutton's cycle

britannica.quote: worn down by water and raised again by subterraneous heat

wikipedia.quote: slow processes seen today, such as erosion and the raising of land

alignments.note: The one theory in the entry that still holds.

alignments.label: No vestige of a beginning

britannica.quote: no vestige of a beginning, no prospect of an end

alignments.note: Right that the earth is far older than anyone thought. It does have a beginning, now dated.

alignments.label: Strata from the deluge

britannica.quote: deposited all at once by the waters of the deluge

wikipedia.quote: Sedimentary rock layers built up slowly over very long periods

alignments.note: The layers took millions of years, not one flood.

alignments.label: Kelvin's estimate

wikipedia.quote: His figure was too low because he did not know about heating by radioactivity

alignments.note: Even the best 19th-century estimates were too young until radioactivity was found.

suggestedQuestions: How old did people in 1797 think the earth was?
Which theory of the earth in 1797 has held up?
What did the 1797 entry think the strata were?

How old did people in 1797 think the ear.answer: Most followed the sacred chronology: created about 4000 years before the Christian era [B2]. Buffon computed about 75,000 years from cooling [B4] [W3], and Hutton saw no vestige of a beginning [B5]. Wikipedia gives 4.54 billion years, from radiometric dating [W1].

Which theory of the earth in 1797 has he.answer: Hutton's. He held that continents are worn down by water and raised again by heat, in a long succession [B5]. Wikipedia credits him with arguing that slow processes seen today shaped the Earth over immense periods [W4]. Burnet's smooth crust [B3], Buffon's comet [B4] and the deluge strata [B6] have not held up [W5] [W6].

What did the 1797 entry think the strata.answer: Layers laid down all at once by the waters of the deluge, in the view of most naturalists [B6]. Wikipedia says sedimentary layers built up slowly over very long periods, and are dated by their order and by radiometric dating of volcanic layers [W6].
